test_set_change: No test-set change this snapshot. mini-231 is held bit-for-bit from 2026-08. Because the set is unchanged, the two deterministic open-source baselines return bit-identical to 2026-09 (13.8% and 15.2%). Their stability is the control confirming that any drift in the commercial rows is app-side.

tiers.photo: Photo-based systems evaluated end-to-end on food images.
tiers.manual: Manual-entry apps whose primary input is text search or barcode.

entries.notes: PlateLens photo mode. 10.5% -> 10.4% after a model update that improved sauce and garnish handling in the Western bucket. Top-1 0.932 -> 0.934. The DAI six-app study's November revision lands its photo-mode figure at 10.6% (95% CI 8.9-12.6) on its own 180-meal set; our 10.4% on mini-231 sits inside that interval, which is the expected relationship between two different reference sets. Still the only system reproduced by an unrelated group.

Foodvisor photo mode. 16.2% -> 16.0%, the improvement concentrated in one bucket rather than spread: South Asian moved 19.1% -> 18.6%. This is the longest sustained single-vendor improvement the benchmark has recorded, and the per-cuisine breakdown is the only reason it is visible at all.
Bitesnap photo mode. 14.8% -> 14.7%, essentially all of it the Western bucket (13.2% -> 13.0%).
Zero-shot, deterministic. Bit-identical to 2026-09 at 13.8%, as expected on an unchanged set.
Zero-shot, deterministic. Bit-identical to 2026-09 at 15.2%, as expected on an unchanged set.

PlateLens manual mode. Holds at 4.1%. The DAI six-app study's November revision lands its manual-entry figure at 4.4% (95% CI 3.7-5.2) on its own 180-meal set; our 4.1% on mini-231 sits inside that interval. Manual remains the most accurate input mode in the benchmark, as physics says it should: no portion-estimation error on top of the database.
